reasons: Classification is correct: Section 13 (p0088) vests all IP in the Work "including any Improvements or Modifications" in Garman, and the only counterbalancing right (p0028) is a non-exclusive, non-transferable object-code licence limited to Authorized Locations with no modify or sublicense right and no perpetual/irrevocable character — that fails the fallback's requirement of a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense customer-funded deliverables, so this is not an acceptable-fallback clause being upgraded.

Redline is minimal and directionally right: it leaves Garman's platform ownership intact (permitted by the detection guidance) and adds only (i) the licence-back over the Modifications and materials developed for and paid for by Sparkling, and (ii) confirmation that Sparkling retains rights in its data, including data converted under Section 4(b) (p0042) — the gap the rationale correctly identifies.
No assignment of Customer IP/data to Vendor is introduced or left standing, and the added no-joint-ownership sentence is belt-and-braces rather than harmful; deterministic checks corroborate.
Comment is accurate, correctly attributed to Section 13 and Section 4, uses the [Playbook] prefix, first-person plural, concise, and expressly offers the fallback rather than demanding assignment.
